parts.title: SPIRAL REVIEW (5 min)
content: 1. SPEAKING FLUENCY: Count the filler words (um, uh, like, you know) in 1 minute of talking about your topic. Target: fewer than 5 filler words per minute.
2. SIGNPOSTING REVISION: Read your presentation script. Are there clear signposts between EVERY section? Add any missing transitions: opening → overview → body → data → conclusion → questions.

3. MATH SPIRAL: Your rehearsal took 12 minutes. The target is 10 minutes. Which section should you shorten? Calculate: if body = 6 min, intro = 2 min, conclusion = 1.5 min, Q&A = 2.5 min, what is the total? Which section can you shorten by 2 minutes?

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Rehearsal is the key to a confident presentation. Professional speakers rehearse 5-10 times before presenting. Each rehearsal improves fluency, timing, and confidence.
content: 📖 Rehearsal is the key to a confident presentation. Professional speakers rehearse 5-10 times before presenting. Each rehearsal improves fluency, timing, and confidence.
The FIRST rehearsal is the most uncomfortable — that is normal! You will stumble over words, forget what comes next, and speak too fast or too slow. This is exactly what rehearsal is for.

During rehearsal, practice these skills: PACING — speak slowly and clearly. A common mistake is rushing when you are nervous. PAUSING — a 2-3 second pause between sections sounds professional and helps the audience process information. EYE CONTACT — look up from your notes every 2-3 sentences. VOLUME — speak loudly enough for everyone in the room to hear.
After your rehearsal, your peer evaluator will give you feedback using a structured rubric. This feedback is a GIFT — it shows you exactly what to work on before the real presentation.
